claim: disrobe reaches normalized opcode-structure agreement for code objects in a 200-module pinned CPython 3.14.5 corpus.
detail: 6077 / 6286 code objects in the pinned 200-module CPython 3.14.5 population have matching normalized opcode structure. All 200 modules occur in the accepted 574-module measurement with the same source and comparator settings. The comparator omits jump targets, most operands, and __annotate__ objects, and does not penalize additional recovered objects. Regression threshold: 96.67%.
gate_source: evidence/results/captured/python-stdlib-full.json records the accepted capture and its pinned subset. crates/disrobe-pass-py-decompile/tests/arbitrary_recompile_gate.rs enforces OBJECT_PCT_FLOOR 96.67 and 124 wholly matching modules. The shared py_arbitrary_measure.py harness defines both populations.

oracle.external: CPython 3.14.5 recompiles the recovered source. The comparator drops jump targets and most operands, removes and merges selected opcodes, omits __annotate__ code objects, and does not reject extra recovered objects; it does not establish semantic or emitted-bytecode equivalence.

title: Python .pyc decompilation, normalized opcode-structure agreement
